title: … name "…" doesn't conform to ….
summary: Used when the name doesn't conform to naming rules associated to its type (constant, variable, class...). pylint calls it invalid-name.
message_templates: {} name "{}" doesn't conform to {}

title: Disallowed name "…".
summary: Used when the name matches bad-names or bad-names-rgxs- (unauthorized names). pylint calls it disallowed-name.
message_templates: Disallowed name "{}"

title: Type variable name does not reflect variance….
summary: Emitted when a TypeVar name doesn't reflect its type variance. According to PEP8, it is recommended to add suffixes '_co' and '_contra' to the variables used to declare covariant or contravariant behaviour respectively. Invariant (default) variables do not require a suffix. The message is also emitted when invariant variables do have a suffix. pylint calls it typevar-name-incorrect-variance.
message_templates: Type variable name does not reflect variance{}

title: Empty … docstring.
summary: Used when a module, function, class or method has an empty docstring (it would be too easy ;). pylint calls it empty-docstring.
message_templates: Empty {} docstring

title: Missing module docstring.
summary: Used when a module has no docstring. Empty modules do not require a docstring. pylint calls it missing-module-docstring.
message_templates: Missing module docstring

title: Missing class docstring.
summary: Used when a class has no docstring. Even an empty class must have a docstring. pylint calls it missing-class-docstring.
message_templates: Missing class docstring

title: Missing function or method docstring.
summary: Used when a function or method has no docstring. Some special methods like __init__ do not require a docstring. pylint calls it missing-function-docstring.
message_templates: Missing function or method docstring

title: Consider changing "…" to "…".
summary: Used when a boolean expression contains an unneeded negation, e.g. when two negation operators cancel each other out. pylint calls it unnecessary-negation.
message_templates: Consider changing "{}" to "{}"

title: Comparison … should be ….
summary: Used when an expression is compared to singleton values like True, False or None. pylint calls it singleton-comparison.
message_templates: Comparison {} should be {}

title: Use isinstance() rather than type() for a typecheck.
summary: The idiomatic way to perform an explicit typecheck in Python is to use isinstance(x, Y) rather than type(x) == Y, type(x) is Y. Though there are unusual situations where these give different results. pylint calls it unidiomatic-typecheck.
message_templates: Use isinstance() rather than type() for a typecheck.

title: TypeVar cannot be both covariant and contravariant.
summary: Emitted when both the "covariant" and "contravariant" keyword arguments are set to "True" in a TypeVar. pylint calls it typevar-double-variance.
message_templates: TypeVar cannot be both covariant and contravariant

title: TypeVar name "…" does not match assigned variable name "…".
summary: Emitted when a TypeVar is assigned to a variable that does not match its name argument. pylint calls it typevar-name-mismatch.
message_templates: TypeVar name "{}" does not match assigned variable name "{}"

title: Consider using enumerate instead of iterating with range and len.
summary: Emitted when code that iterates with range and len is encountered. Such code can be simplified by using the enumerate builtin. pylint calls it consider-using-enumerate.
message_templates: Consider using enumerate instead of iterating with range and len

title: Consider iterating the dictionary directly instead of calling .keys().
summary: Emitted when the keys of a dictionary are iterated through the .keys() method or when .keys() is used for a membership check. It is enough to iterate through the dictionary itself, for key in dictionary. For membership checks, if key in dictionary is faster. pylint calls it consider-iterating-dictionary.
message_templates: Consider iterating the dictionary directly instead of calling .keys()

title: Class method … should have … as first argument.
summary: Used when a class method has a first argument named differently than the value specified in valid-classmethod-first-arg option (default to "cls"), recommended to easily differentiate them from regular instance methods. pylint calls it bad-classmethod-argument.
message_templates: Class method {} should have {} as first argument

title: Metaclass method … should have … as first argument.
summary: Used when a metaclass method has a first argument named differently than the value specified in valid-classmethod-first-arg option (default to "cls"), recommended to easily differentiate them from regular instance methods. pylint calls it bad-mcs-method-argument.
message_templates: Metaclass method {} should have {} as first argument

title: Metaclass class method … should have … as first argument.
summary: Used when a metaclass class method has a first argument named differently than the value specified in valid-metaclass-classmethod-first-arg option (default to "mcs"), recommended to easily differentiate them from regular instance methods. pylint calls it bad-mcs-classmethod-argument.
message_templates: Metaclass class method {} should have {} as first argument

title: Class __slots__ should be a non-string iterable.
summary: Used when a class __slots__ is a simple string, rather than an iterable. pylint calls it single-string-used-for-slots.
message_templates: Class __slots__ should be a non-string iterable

title: Consider iterating with .items().
summary: Emitted when iterating over the keys of a dictionary and accessing the value by index lookup. Both the key and value can be accessed by iterating using the .items() method of the dictionary instead. pylint calls it consider-using-dict-items.
message_templates: Consider iterating with .items()

title: Use … instead.
summary: Emitted when accessing only the first or last element of str.split(). The first and last element can be accessed by using str.split(sep, maxsplit=1)[0] or str.rsplit(sep, maxsplit=1)[-1] instead. pylint calls it use-maxsplit-arg.
message_templates: Use {} instead

title: Use a sequence type when iterating over values.
summary: When iterating over values, sequence types (e.g., lists, tuples, ranges) are more efficient than sets. pylint calls it use-sequence-for-iteration.
message_templates: Use a sequence type when iterating over values

title: Formatting a regular string which could be an f-string.
summary: Used when we detect a string that is being formatted with format() or % which could potentially be an f-string. The use of f-strings is preferred. Requires Python 3.6 and py-version >= 3.6. pylint calls it consider-using-f-string.
message_templates: Formatting a regular string which could be an f-string

title: Line too long (…/…).
summary: Used when a line is longer than a given number of characters. pylint calls it line-too-long.
message_templates: Line too long ({}/{})

title: Too many lines in module (…/…).
summary: Used when a module has too many lines, reducing its readability. pylint calls it too-many-lines.

title: Trailing whitespace.
summary: Used when there is whitespace between the end of a line and the newline. pylint calls it trailing-whitespace.

title: Final newline missing.
summary: Used when the last line in a file is missing a newline. pylint calls it missing-final-newline.

title: Trailing newlines.
summary: Used when there are trailing blank lines in a file. pylint calls it trailing-newlines.
